title: Is CONTROL Resonant a Sequel?
excerpt: How Dylan Faden's story connects to CONTROL, and why Remedy also calls it a new entry point.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant returns to the same paranatural universe, but moves the action beyond the Oldest House and puts Dylan Faden at the center of the story.
quickAnswer: Yes. Remedy describes CONTROL Resonant as a direct sequel to CONTROL (2019). It is also designed as a new entry point, so the first game is useful context rather than a prerequisite.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden carrying the shapeshifting Aberrant above warped Manhattan in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: Is CONTROL Resonant a direct sequel?
paragraphs: CONTROL Resonant is the next main entry in the Control universe and follows the events of the original game. Remedy has used both “sequel” and “new entry point” to describe it: the story continues, but it is built to stand on its own.

sections.title: How CONTROL Resonant Connects to CONTROL
paragraphs: The first game followed Jesse Faden inside the Oldest House. Resonant reverses that direction. The lockdown is failing, the crisis has reached Manhattan, and Dylan leaves the Bureau's headquarters to face what is spreading outside.

Jesse remains central to the story, but Remedy has confirmed that Dylan is the only playable character. His search for his missing sister connects the siblings' stories without repeating Jesse's journey.

sections.title: What Changes in the Sequel
bullets: A larger, zone-based Manhattan replaces the mostly interior focus of the Oldest House.
Combat is built around the shapeshifting melee weapon called the Aberrant.
Supernatural Combat Abilities, Talents, Artifacts, and weapon forms create a deeper action-RPG progression system.
Dylan's Journey forms the main campaign, while World Quests provide self-contained stories.

sections.title: Do You Need to Play CONTROL First?
paragraphs: No. Remedy says Resonant can be a player's first step into the series. Playing CONTROL will still add context for Dylan, Jesse, the Hiss, the Federal Bureau of Control, and the Oldest House, so returning players are likely to notice more of the connections.

title: Should You Play CONTROL Before CONTROL Resonant?
excerpt: The short answer for newcomers, plus the story context returning players will already know.
introduction: Resonant is tied closely to the Faden siblings and the Federal Bureau of Control, but Remedy has deliberately built the sequel for both returning players and newcomers.
quickAnswer: You do not need to play CONTROL first. Remedy says Resonant stands on its own, though the original gives useful background on Dylan, Jesse, the Hiss, and the Oldest House.
imageAlt: The interior of the Oldest House in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: Do you need to play CONTROL first?
paragraphs: Start with Resonant if its Manhattan setting and melee-focused combat are what interest you. The game is written as a fresh entry point and does not require a completed CONTROL save.

sections.title: What the First Game Adds
bullets: Why Jesse entered the Oldest House and became Director of the FBC.
How Dylan was held by the Bureau and affected by the Hiss.
The nature of the Oldest House, Objects of Power, and paranatural containment.
The emotional history behind Jesse and Dylan's search for one another.

sections.title: Why Resonant Still Works as a Starting Point
paragraphs: Resonant changes protagonist, location, combat focus, and scale. Dylan emerges into Manhattan during a new cosmic crisis, meets characters such as FBC field agent Zoe De Vera, and learns systems that were not part of Jesse's original campaign.
That structure gives the sequel room to explain what Dylan needs to know when he needs to know it, instead of expecting every player to remember the 2019 story.

sections.title: Our Recommendation
paragraphs: Play CONTROL first if you enjoy story mysteries and have time before September 24. If not, watch an official story recap or begin with Resonant; the developers explicitly support that choice.

title: CONTROL Resonant Editions and Pre-order Bonuses
excerpt: Standard, Digital Deluxe, physical, and SteelBook editions compared with the latest release timing.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant is sold digitally in Standard and Digital Deluxe editions, with Standard and SteelBook physical options for consoles. The physical release follows the digital launch.
quickAnswer: Choose Standard for the complete base game. Digital Deluxe adds the digital artbook, soundtrack, AWE Mission Outfit, Untapped Artifact (Wallet), and a Starter Resource Bundle; PlayStation also lists 48-hour early access. No Collector's Edition is planned. Physical console editions release October 15, 2026.
imageAlt: Warped Manhattan skyline used in official CONTROL Resonant promotional art

sections.title: Which CONTROL Resonant edition should you buy?
paragraphs: The base game is included in every announced edition. Deluxe extras are digital bonuses, while the SteelBook edition is a separate physical package for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Pricing and availability can vary by region and retailer.

sections.title: Pre-order Bonuses
paragraphs: Steam lists the Hiss Corruption Outfit and Pickpocket's Tool Artifact for pre-purchase customers. The US PlayStation Store lists those two items plus the Occult Outfit. Store terms can differ by platform and region, so verify the bonus line on the exact listing where you plan to buy.
These are cosmetic or progression items, not story expansions. Remedy describes the base game as a complete launch experience.

sections.title: Digital Deluxe Early Access
paragraphs: The PlayStation Store advertises up to 48 hours of early access with Digital Deluxe, which points to September 22 on PS5. Do not assume the same timing on another platform unless its own store page states it.

sections.title: Physical Release Timing
paragraphs: Remedy moved the physical console release to October 15, 2026, while the digital release remains September 24. Retail delivery dates can be later than the publisher date.

sections.title: Is there a Collector's Edition?
paragraphs: No. Remedy's developer-pinned FAQ says a Collector's Edition is not planned. The SteelBook package is the premium physical option currently announced, but it should not be relabeled as a Collector's Edition.

title: CONTROL Resonant PC System Requirements
excerpt: Official minimum, recommended, ray tracing, and path tracing PC specifications in one clear guide.
introduction: Remedy published the final PC requirements on September 9. Every tier requires 16 GB of RAM, Windows 10 or 11 64-bit, and 120 GB of SSD space.
quickAnswer: For 1080p at 30 FPS on Low, Remedy lists a GTX 1070, RX 5600 XT, or Arc A580 with 6 GB VRAM and an i5-8500 or Ryzen 5 3500. The 1440p/60 recommended tier moves to an RTX 3060 Ti, RX 6700 XT, or Arc B580 with 8 GB VRAM.
imageAlt: Official CONTROL Resonant PC requirements chart from Remedy Entertainment

sections.title: What PC hardware does CONTROL Resonant require?
paragraphs: The minimum tier targets 1080p/30 with a Quality upscaler and Low graphics. Recommended targets 1440p/60 with Balanced upscaling and Medium graphics. Frame Generation was not used for Remedy's test configurations.

sections.title: How to read the performance tiers

subsections.title: Match resolution and graphics settings
paragraphs: A recommended GPU is tied to a target, not every setting. Compare resolution, preset and upscaler mode before choosing a tier.

subsections.title: Separate capacity from performance
paragraphs: Meeting RAM and storage requirements does not establish that a GPU can deliver the highest ray-tracing tier.

subsections.title: Use the final chart
paragraphs: The early FAQ lists initial requirements. The newer September announcement is the specification used below.

title: Is CONTROL Resonant on Game Pass?
excerpt: The latest launch status, and why Xbox Play Anywhere does not mean Game Pass.
introduction: CONTROL Resonant has an Xbox release and Xbox Play Anywhere support, but those are separate from an Xbox Game Pass subscription listing.
quickAnswer: No Game Pass launch has been announced as of September 15, 2026. CONTROL Resonant is confirmed for Xbox Series X|S and Xbox on PC with Xbox Play Anywhere, but Play Anywhere is not the same as Game Pass.
imageAlt: Dylan Faden fighting Hiss-corrupted enemies in CONTROL Resonant

sections.title: Is CONTROL Resonant coming to Game Pass?
paragraphs: The official Xbox and Remedy announcements describe a paid release and highlight Xbox Play Anywhere. Neither announcement says CONTROL Resonant joins Game Pass on day one.

sections.title: Xbox Play Anywhere vs Game Pass
paragraphs: Xbox Play Anywhere lets a qualifying digital purchase work across Xbox console and Xbox on PC, with shared saves, add-ons, and achievements. Game Pass is a subscription catalog. A game can support one without being included in the other.

sections.title: Confirmed Xbox Launch Options
bullets: Xbox Series X|S digital release on September 24, 2026

Physical Xbox release on October 15, 2026
Standard and Digital Deluxe purchasing options, depending on storefront

sections.title: What Could Change
paragraphs: A later Game Pass agreement is always possible, but there is no basis to treat it as confirmed. This page will change only when Remedy or Xbox publishes a subscription announcement.

title: Does CONTROL Resonant Use Denuvo?
excerpt: What the Steam listing currently discloses—and what remains unconfirmed before launch.
introduction: DRM questions need a storefront disclosure or publisher statement. At present, the official PC pages do not provide enough evidence for a definite yes or no.
quickAnswer: Denuvo has not been confirmed for CONTROL Resonant as of September 15, 2026. The Steam page does not currently display a Denuvo notice, but absence of that notice before release is not proof that the game is DRM-free.
imageAlt: Dylan facing a giant face-like entity amid floating debris in official CONTROL Resonant media

sections.title: Is Denuvo confirmed for CONTROL Resonant?
paragraphs: There is currently no official Denuvo confirmation. Treat claims that it definitely has—or definitely does not have—Denuvo as unverified until Remedy or a storefront adds a clear disclosure.

sections.title: What the Steam Page Shows
paragraphs: Steam lists the release date, supported features, languages, editions, and PC requirements. The page checked for this guide did not include a third-party Denuvo anti-tamper notice.

sections.title: Why the Answer Is Still Unconfirmed
paragraphs: Store disclosures can be updated close to release, and the presence or absence of one line is weaker evidence than a direct publisher statement. We therefore record the status as unconfirmed instead of turning a missing label into a promise.

sections.title: What to Check at Launch
bullets: The third-party DRM disclosure on the Steam store page
The final Steam subscriber agreement shown before purchase
Any PC technical FAQ published by Remedy
Post-launch executable behavior reported by reputable PC outlets

sections.title: What About the Original CONTROL on Switch?
paragraphs: The original game reached Nintendo Switch as a cloud version. That history shows the series has appeared on Nintendo hardware, but it does not confirm a native or cloud edition of Resonant.

sections.title: When This Status Changes
paragraphs: A Switch 2 version should be considered real only after Remedy, Nintendo, or an official store publishes it. Hardware speculation and retailer placeholders are not confirmation.
